thread:
Victor (Customer): Hey team, hitting intermittent 429s from our production app since last night. We send requests through a NATed egress (single public IP) and also include a per-project API key in X-Api-Key. Billing shows no overage for our project/org. Any idea why we're getting 429s?

Maya (Support): sorry to hear that — can you paste a failing curl and the exact 429 response body? Also what's the public NAT IP and the api key prefix (no full keys) so we can look up logs?

Victor (Customer): repro curl:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-abc123" -H "X-Api-Key: proj_9X3" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
429 response: `\{"error\":\{"type\":\"rate_limit\",\"reason\":\"rate_limited\",\"scope\":\"org\"\}\}`
NAT IP: 54.210.33.77
Billing: project shows 3M tokens this month which is within limit.

Maya (Support): thanks — forwarding to SRE with logs. @Jordan can you check how the quota engine attributed these requests? Victor, we're keeping this thread for updates. :eyes: 

Jordan (SRE): looking — pulling up attribution for IP 54.210.33.77 and api key proj_9X3. Quick note: quota engine applies limits in priority order: API key -> project -> org -> egress-IP aggregation (we also have a short-window burst controller keyed by NAT IP for DDoS protection).

Jordan (SRE): I see a burst of short 1000 req/min from that IP across multiple keys around 02:14 UTC. The engine flagged the NAT IP burst throttler (1s buckets, 50 req/s soft limit). The requests for your API key were under project quota, but the NAT-level burst rule tripped and responded with 429 scope=org to simplify clients. 

Victor (Customer): ah got it — so even if our project quota is fine, the NAT burst rule can still 429 us? That seems odd because it impacts unrelated projects behind same IP. We share the IP with partner services.

Ben (Eng): we intentionally return a generic scope sometimes to avoid leaking mapping info. But we can surface more precise reasons for support-facing logs. For customer-facing 429s we usually annotate with `x-rate-scope` header (we might not always expose internal NAT triggers). Victor, did the 429 include an `x-rate-limit-reset` header?

Victor (Customer): no reset header present in responses we've captured. Just the JSON error above.

Jordan (SRE): looks like the NAT burst controller path didn't populate the reset header — bug. Two actions: (1) short-term: we can add an allowlist exception for your org IP+key combo to bypass NAT burst throttler (we've applied a temporary exception tied to proj_9X3 and org:victor-co until 2026-03-20 23:59 UTC), (2) long-term: eng to change response headers to include `x-rate-limit-reset` and a clearer `x-rate-scope=ip` when NAT controller triggers.

Maya (Support): Victor — we've added the temporary exception and will monitor for 30m. Please confirm if 429s stop.

Victor (Customer): just tested — no 429s in the last 5m, latency looks normal. Thank you! 

Ratebot: [automated] applied exception id ex-2026-78 for proj_9X3 (expires 2026-03-20T23:59:00Z).

Ben (Eng): filing a ticket for the header bug and scope clarity: ENG-6421. Plan: (a) ensure NAT-burst responses include `x-rate-scope=ip` and `x-rate-limit-reset` and `x-rate-limit-remaining`, (b) add telemetry so support can see exact rule that fired without exposing buckets to customers. Also evaluate moving NAT burst logic to a per-customer weighted bucket to reduce collateral impact.

Jordan (SRE): FYI for the team: root cause was a simultaneous backup job from another tenant that spiked egress from that NAT for ~3m. Quota engine correctly protected the cluster but collateral 429s were user-visible; that's why we need the per-customer weight.

Maya (Support): escalation complete. Victor if anything reoccurs ping me here and we'll escalate to oncall. I'll keep ENG-6421 linked to this thread. :white_check_mark:

Victor (Customer): appreciate the quick action. Can you also confirm this won't cause billing anomalies? We didn't use extra tokens.

Jordan (SRE): the temporary exception doesn't change billing; it's purely a throttle bypass. We saw no token overage. I'll add a note to the ticket to confirm billing data.

Ben (Eng): leaving a small follow-up: we'll also add a dashboard alert for high NAT fanout that triggers product alerts so we can proactively reassign NATs or request vendor help.

Maya (Support): closing the loop here in 24h unless Victor asks to keep open. Marking as resolved for now. :lock: 

Victor (Customer): sounds good, thanks everyone.

---
Internal notes appended to thread by Maya (Support):
- Repro steps provided by customer; verified 429s were NAT-burst related.
- Temporary exception applied ex-2026-78.
- ENG-6421 created to: populate headers + reduce collateral impact + add telemetry + confirm billing neutrality.
- SRE to monitor NAT IP 54.210.33.77 for 48h.
